TAVI-AGENT-005.title: Native Tavi channel contract for OpenClaw
TAVI-AGENT-005.summary: Review the current upstream OpenClaw channel plugin lifecycle, installation manifest, message routing and ack contracts; design Tavi as a generic client endpoint using ordinary Social user auth. No LoopRD/OpenClaw-only server dependency.
checks: Use a pinned, inspected official OpenClaw channel plugin SDK revision and a real example plugin; document actual package exports, entrypoints, lifecycle hooks and version compatibility, without inventing an API.

Specify mapping of Tavi server origin, Tavi account ID, peer/group conversation IDs, signed-in session and inbound/outbound OpenClaw message envelopes; distinguish platform identity from display names.
Specify reliable wake/catch-up, cursor/idempotency and authenticated replay behavior, shutdown/restart cleanup and bounded history. Explicitly document any at-least-once limitations.
Produce a testable, installable native channel scaffold and a design that does not change Tavi general messaging semantics or require OpenClaw on the Social server.

TAVI-AGENT-006.title: OpenClaw native channel for ordinary Tavi messaging
TAVI-AGENT-006.summary: Build a properly installed OpenClaw native channel, not an external forever-running CLI bridge; receive/send authenticated Tavi DMs and supported events through shared SDK. Game challenges remain ordinary Tavi interactions; group support is feature gated until SCL-007.
checks: Install and enable the native Tavi channel through OpenClaw plugin management; connect one dedicated ordinary Tavi account with private credentials and no privileged Social or LoopRD service token.
Human -> Tavi DM -> OpenClaw agent -> Tavi reply works with independent per-peer session routing and sender display-name metadata; outgoing messages are sent by the authenticated agent account.

Contact invitations and game.challenge.requested/response events reach the right agent account as typed events; manual acceptance and opt-in peer/game allowlisted automatic acceptance use the normal Social APIs, with no game seat grants.
Groups are supported only when Tavi group APIs and ACLs actually exist; unsupported group capabilities are advertised as unavailable rather than simulated.
Channel starts/stops/reconnects with OpenClaw, uses replay-safe bounded reconciliation and does not require tavi-openclaw-service.mjs to run.

TAVI-AGENT-007.title: Native Tavi channel security, migration and live acceptance
TAVI-AGENT-007.summary: Cross-device, restart, account isolation and resilience QA of the native OpenClaw channel, then operator-approved optional retirement of external watcher; preserve CLI fallback until native parity proven.
checks: Using two human Tavi accounts and one separately authenticated OpenClaw account, demonstrate DM both directions and a challenged game acceptance entirely through native OpenClaw channel (external watcher disabled).

Verify authorization for accepted/unaccepted contacts, per-account isolation, event recipient scoping, allowlist enforcement, malicious inbound message containment and no credential in logs, prompts or outbound game URLs.

Stop/restart OpenClaw and disable network during pending messages/challenges; verify bounded catch-up, no unrecoverable loss within server retention, no runaway duplicate sends and explicit limitation documentation.
Confirm native plugin installation/upgrades and downgrade/rollback; only then propose disabling external watcher, without deleting CLI support or changing ordinary Tavi clients.
Operator reviews actual OpenClaw Gateway runtime traces, Tavi inbox messages, Windows UI and server-side authorization logs before marking Done.

TAVI-MULTI-047.title: Life authoritative match creation and OpenClaw turn adapter
TAVI-MULTI-047.summary: Cross-repository dependency: Life, not Tavi or OpenClaw channel, creates and persists matches after accepted Tavi challenge; verifies Tavi identity proof and per-game seat; exposes legal actions and executes agent turns without UI automation.
TAVI-MULTI-047.owner: Life backend + game adapter (coordination only in Social)
checks: Life provides reviewed authenticated create/join/resume, inspect, legal_actions, act and end_turn endpoints with durable match IDs, validated Tavi subject-to-seat bindings and idempotent command IDs.
An accepted Tavi challenge is correlated to one operator-approved Life match; rejection/expiry/replay creates no seat and no game action, and match admission always requires Life authorization.
OpenClaw uses a game-specific legal-action adapter via independent Tavi identity and Life API; cannot act for another player, invent moves or bypass legal-action validation.
Two participants can disconnect, resume and complete legal Life turns; changes to match seats and closed state trigger accurate Social roster and notification updates.
Game backend changes are tracked and approved in the Life project workboard; this Tavi item records the dependency and integration evidence, not a claim of Life implementation.

TAVI-MULTI-048.title: End-to-end Tavi, Atrium and Life multiplayer acceptance
TAVI-MULTI-048.summary: Prove the requested human-vs-OpenClaw and two-human hostless matches from Windows Tavi through Atrium/Life, including restart/resume, private match chat, server-owned rules and notifications.
checks: Windows Tavi shows Life, user chooses Challenge against OpenClaw, native channel receives and accepts the invitation, and Life creates a verified playable match whose ID can be launched/resumed via Atrium.
Human plays legal turns versus OpenClaw, OpenClaw observes its own authorized seat and plays via Life game API, and the game progresses to a final state without a continuously connected host.
Open same match from another device after app/agent/backend restart; match and turns persist and all clients agree on the authoritative game state.
Verify two human players can also create/join/complete a game and private match conversation ACLs follow actual Life roster removal and closure.
Attempt replay, unauthorized seat access, expired invitations and stale/duplicate actions; all fail safely with no credential leakage. Obtain explicit operator sign-off.

Associate post-update command outcomes with the exact v0.3.46 artifact SHA cb837d71f5d04731ea9c6c5f1ec5c0db0a7d5e71cbafd616944c40c61f141615. Reject evidence from any different ZIP SHA or stale run.

Operator confirms CI/ZIP evidence and only then approves ticket status; never infer device acceptance or grant permission to push/release.
